note.question: How do user privacy concerns affect competition between online advertising platforms?
note.overview: This paper studies the effect of user privacy concerns on competition between online advertising platforms. Online platforms attract advertisers by offering capabilities to reach audiences likely to be receptive to their ads in a timely and accurate manner. However, the collection and processing of user information required for targeting of ads may lead to privacy concerns.

source.quote: We study the effect of user privacy concerns on competition between online advertising platforms.
We study the effect of user privacy concerns on competition between online advertising platforms.
Online platforms attract advertisers by offering capabilities to reach audiences likely to be receptive to their ads in a timely and accurate manner.
The presence of heterogeneity in the user and the advertiser populations with respect to their preferences for targeting leads to differentiation between platforms.
On the other hand, only 38% of users in the age group of 55+ prefer to see relevant ads, based on browsing history, over random ads.
Both platforms have access to the same cost function.

In addition, for simplicity, we also assume that while an advertiser’s gain from using a platform depends on the number of users on the platform, the utility of a user does not vary with the number of advertisers on the platform.
We model the competition between two platforms as a two-stage game where platforms announce their targeting capabilities in the first stage and advertising fees in the second stage.
